observations: Photo 0: Silver-and-black retro-style mirrorless body with 'Nikon' and 'Zfc' engravings visible on top plate; front body cap reads 'Nikon Z mount'.
Photo 1: Close-up of a manual-focus lens mounted on the body; aperture/focus rings visible with numeric markings; ISO dial shows 'Zfc' label.
Photo 2: Top-down shot of full camera with lens attached, plus a Nikon-branded battery, Nikon battery charger, two rear body/lens caps, and a front lens cap printed 'TTArtisan APS-C 25mm F2.0'.
No photo shows the camera powered on, a screen display, serial number plate, or shutter count.
No memory card, strap, or box shown.

identity.model: Z fc (with TTArtisan 25mm F2.0 APS-C lens)

claims.claim: Nikon Z fc is a retro-inspired, SLR-style mirrorless camera with a 20.9-megapixel APS-C sensor
claims.evidence: Body badge confirms model name (photo 0, photo 1), but sensor resolution and functionality cannot be confirmed from static photos.

risks.risk: Camera may not power on or sensor may be faulty
risks.proof: Video of camera powering on, showing live view/EVF image and menu screen

risks.risk: High shutter count or heavy prior use
risks.proof: Screenshot of shutter count from camera menu or third-party shutter-count tool

risks.risk: Lens (TTArtisan 25mm F2.0) may have scratches, fungus, or focus ring stiffness not visible in current close-ups
risks.proof: Clear macro photos of front and rear glass elements under light
risks.if_unproven: priced as lens condition unverified/cosmetic only

risks.proof: Screenshot of battery info/cycle count from camera menu
Clear photo of serial number plate (bottom plate) matching Nikon registration format

proof_requests: Video of camera powering on with menu/shutter count visible
Clear photo of serial number plate on base of camera
Macro shots of lens front/rear elements for scratches or fungus
Screenshot of battery cycle count or battery health
Any memory card/image sample from the camera to confirm sensor function
response.reason: The camera body (Nikon Z fc) and attached lens (TTArtisan 25mm F2.0) are both clearly identifiable from the photos, so pricing can proceed at worst-case condition absent proof of working order, shutter count, lens glass condition, and authenticity.
